UseCaseID: Title: Automation and Centralized Management of Spending Authorization Forms (SAFs)
Title: Automation and Centralized Management of Spending Authorization Forms (SAFs)
Overview: In accordance with Financial Administration Manual (FAM) Chapter 1014-4-1, Sections 4.0 to 6.0, and the Delegation of Authorities for Financial Administration, a Spending Authorization Form (SAF) is required to authorize a Responsibility Centre (RC) Manager to expend funds against another RC Manager's budget.  Currently, SAFs are completed and signed manually, with responsibility for document retention resting with the respective RC Managers. Each authorization is valid for a maximum of one year.  This initiative seeks to modernize the existing SAF process through automation and centralized information management, enabling improved financial oversight, document retention, compliance monitoring, and audit readiness within the VCDS Group.
Business Problem: The current SAF process is decentralized and relies heavily on manual administration, with limited oversight and no centralized mechanism to record, track, or monitor spending authorizations.  Once an SAF has been signed by the respective RC Managers, the parties are responsible for retaining copies of the authorization. However, there is no centralized repository or tracking mechanism to provide the VCDS Comptroller with visibility over active, expired, or superseded SAFs.  This creates several administrative and financial management challenges:  Limited visibility over which RC Managers have been authorized to expend funds against other RC budgets.  No automated mechanism to monitor the one-year validity period or identify SAFs approaching expiration.  Inconsistent document retention and potential difficulties retrieving supporting documentation for financial verification, compliance reviews, and audits.  Increased administrative burden associated with manually completing, distributing, tracking, and renewing SAFs.  Limited ability for the VCDS Comptroller to conduct proactive oversight and verify that appropriate spending authorizations are documented and remain valid.  Although SAFs are widely used, the absence of centralized oversight creates potential internal control weaknesses and limits the Comptroller's ability to effectively monitor compliance with financial administration requirements.
Desired Outcome: Develop and implement an automated, centralized SAF management solution that improves administrative efficiency, strengthens internal financial controls, and enhances oversight of spending authorizations within the VCDS Group.  The proposed solution should ideally provide the following capabilities:  Digital Workflow: Enable RC Managers to initiate, review, approve, and renew SAFs through a standardized electronic process.  Centralized Repository: Establish a secure, accessible repository containing all SAFs, including authorization details, effective dates, expiration dates, and supporting documentation.  Automated Tracking and Notifications: Monitor SAF validity periods and generate notifications for upcoming expirations, renewals, and outstanding approvals.  Management Oversight: Provide the VCDS Comptroller with a consolidated view of active, expired, and pending SAFs to facilitate monitoring and compliance verification.  Audit Trail and Document Retention: Maintain historical records of SAF approvals, amendments, renewals, and expirations to support financial audits, verification activities, and applicable records management requirements.  Reporting Capabilities: Enable the generation of reports identifying authorized RC Managers, associated RC budgets, authorization periods, and overall compliance status.

Overview: CANMILREP produces a recurring bilingual weekly Situation Report (SITREP) that is submitted by the Military Representative to NATO directly to the CDS. The current process requires collecting inputs from multiple Staff Officers, consolidating information, coordinating revisions through the Chief of Staff, obtaining approval from the Military Representative and distributing the final product to a large and evolving audience of senior leadership stakeholders. Although initially focused on the weekly SITREP process, the platform could be expanded to support other recurring executive reporting requirements across CANMILREP and the VCDS enterprise.

Distribution lists consisting primarily of General and Flag Officers require constant maintenance and validation. Producing bilingual versions increases workload and introduces opportunities for discrepancies between language products. The overall process lacks real-time visibility regarding report readiness, outstanding actions, approval status and dissemination, resulting in administrative burden that reduces the time available for higher-value operational analysis and decision support activities.

Title: SOCD Automation
Overview: The SOCD process is a critical administrative and operational function that requires the coordination of multiple stakeholders, documents, approvals, and status updates. Currently, members often rely on email chains, spreadsheets, and manual follow-ups to determine the status of their SOCD submission, resulting in inefficiencies, delays, and limited visibility for both applicants and leadership. This proposal seeks to develop a centralized digital SOCD tracking and workflow management solution that provides end-to-end visibility from submission to completion. The solution would automate task assignment, track progress in real time, generate reminders for outstanding actions, and provide dashboards for supervisors and decision-makers. The objective is to create a simple, user-friendly platform that improves the member experience, reduces administrative burden, and accelerates overall SOCD processing times.
Business Problem: The current SOCD process can be difficult for members and administrators to navigate due to the reliance on manual tracking methods and fragmented communication channels. Common challenges include:  Members have limited visibility into the status of their SOCD request. Applicants often need to send emails or contact multiple stakeholders to obtain updates. Action items can be delayed when ownership is unclear or when tasks are overlooked. Administrative staff spend considerable time responding to status inquiries and conducting manual follow-ups. Supervisors have limited real-time visibility into the overall SOCD workload and processing timelines. Bottlenecks are difficult to identify until delays have already occurred. Leadership lacks centralized reporting on the number of active SOCDs, processing times, and overdue actions.  As a result, the process can become time-consuming for members, resource-intensive for administrators, and difficult for leadership to monitor effectively.
Desired Outcome: The desired outcome is a modern, centralized digital solution that streamlines the SOCD process from submission through completion. Improved Member Experience Members would have access to a simple and intuitive portal where they can:  Submit SOCD requests electronically. View the current status of their request at any time. See where their file is within the approval process. Receive automatic updates when actions are completed. Reduce the need for email inquiries and manual follow-up.  This provides greater transparency and confidence while significantly reducing uncertainty throughout the process. Faster Processing Times The solution would automate workflow routing and task assignments, ensuring requests are immediately directed to the appropriate stakeholder. Automated reminders and notifications would:  Reduce delays caused by missed emails. Ensure action items are completed on time. Escalate overdue tasks when necessary. Keep files moving through the process without requiring manual intervention.  By reducing administrative friction, overall SOCD turnaround times can be shortened. Increased Visibility for Supervisors and Leadership Supervisors and decision-makers would gain access to real-time dashboards displaying:  Total SOCD requests in progress. Current stage of each file. Average processing times. Outstanding actions. Overdue files. Workload distribution across staff.  This would provide leadership with immediate situational awareness and enable proactive intervention when delays occur. Enhanced Accountability Each SOCD request would have clearly defined ownership throughout the process. The system would track:  Who currently has the file. When it was assigned. Pending actions. Completion dates. Historical status changes.  This creates transparency, improves accountability, and reduces the risk of requests being lost or delayed.

A Power Apps canvas app has been developed to provide users with a centralized interface for managing parking requests, vehicle records, and allocation data.

Title: Use of AI Tools for Semantic Analysis in Policy Contradiction Research
Overview:
We are conducting a project focused on identifying contradictions between DND/CAF Information and IT Security Policy Instruments. This includes, but is not limited to, DAODs, NDSODs, ITSS, IMS, and relevant TBS/CSE policy instruments.

As part of this initiative, we are exploring the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to support semantic analysis for contradiction detection. Specifically, we are looking at using AI tools to compare any two policy documents and find parts that might contradict each other, not just by looking for specific words, but by understanding the actual meaning of the sentences. 

General feasibility of using AI for semantic analysis: can the AI tool chunk/segment different sections of a policy document and then compare those segments to that of other policy documents, to identify any contradictions?
Business Problem: Can AI, in combination with Microsoft Power Platform tools, be leveraged to automatically identify and document semantic contradictions across DND/CAF Information and IT Security Policy Instruments? These instruments include, but are not limited to, DAODs, NDSODs, ITSS, IMS, and relevant TBS/CSE policy instruments.
Desired Outcome:
A well-structured and comprehensive document that presents all identified contradictions across DND/CAF Information and IT Security Policy Instruments. This document will include:

- Contradiction Mapping: Clear identification and categorization of contradictions and inconsistencies found within and across policy documents.


- Highlighting of policy instruments with the highest frequency or severity of contradictions, to guide focused review and remediation efforts.

- Policy Groupings: Clustering of documents based on shared or overlapping content, enabling more efficient comparison and analysis of contradictions within these related sets.
Current Roadblocks: Tools we need access to: PowerApps, Power Automate, AI Hub/AI Builder, Copilot Studio (optional)
